cells.tense: The instrument is picking up the signal with the pen down and clear.
cells.ask: Write down what has been pulling you and not yet arrived. First line that comes.
cells.core:
You're in real contact with the pull — you can feel the difference between wanting a thing and being wanted by it, and you move with the second kind. Plans get made out of it. Questions get asked out loud. What's rare here is how clean it stays: a direction lands in you like something remembered rather than figured out.

The appetite is doing the work. Someone who is a beginner at the thing they love. That's not new at it — it's open to it. And what keeps the appetite fed is fuel, not rest: the next step that's a little more than the last one. Move before the steps are laid out, once this week, on the thing that keeps floating back up.
cells.sheetLine: The pull is clear and you're moving with it.
cells.verb: Meeting the unknown ahead of you with fresh wonder.
cells.place: Standing under the direction you're already being pulled toward.

cells.tense: You are living in a version of this that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's pulling you and do its next small step today. One, only.
cells.core:
You're ahead of where this actually is. Every question in front of you gets answered three moves further out — what it'll mean, who'll approve, what happens after — and the questions that were about now get dropped. Nothing has arrived yet and the future is getting your best attention.

That push comes from wanting it so much. About facing what's already in your hands? You can tell yourself you're keeping the vision alive. The vision doesn't need keeping.

The move back is closer to where you are. Act on the next step of one thing, today, small. Not the whole plan. Just the next piece.

cells.tense: Something behind you keeps the hand off the string.
cells.ask: Listen to one person for ten minutes without offering a thing back.
cells.core:
The instrument sits right there — you've known where it is for a while. It just isn't sounding. Decisions get called practical. A question about what you actually want answers itself with a list of what's reasonable. Nobody put the hand down for you.

You don't need more vision. What's worn through is knowing which of the wants is real. So start close in: one thing you can't prove yet — you feel it as right and can't say why. Find one small true thing and follow just that, today, where checking is small.

Hear someone fully first. Not to fix it. Just to hear it. One person, ten minutes, no advice.

cells.tense: The pen is moving in you and it is not being called yours.
cells.ask: When someone asks, answer what you want straight and stop giving reasons.
cells.core:
You're already following the pull — that's why certain rooms light you up and certain invitations you keep turning down. But you describe those as circumstance, timing, the work. Your reach keeps pointing at something, and you keep filing it under other things.

Feel where it lands. The direction shows up as a skip in the chest, a room you linger in, a subject you keep drifting back to. That's the instrument, and you've been treating what it gives you as background noise.

Say one of them straight, out loud, to one person. Say it small and true. Then let them hear it. Just say it.

attempts.check: The record does not say what the person goes wide-eyed toward — their star's content is theirs; I render the reaching, never an object I invented. A reader could object that this is a single beginner's moment, so each cell locates its own moment they can refuse (what they say at answers, in use, at an open thing) and keeps the ask usable even if the moment is wrong. The ask is one physical act, repeats each time in other words, and writes no promise; the sentence that served me — the first-timer facing unknown depths — is cut before the cells, and the Dreamer and heart stay off the page.

attempts.check: The record does not say what the person is drawn toward — the star's content is theirs, so I render the reaching and never an object I invented. A reader could object that each cell assumes they already feel a pull at all; each moment is locatable and refusable (what they say at answers, in use, at an open thing), and the asks stand alone as useful acts even if my read is off. The sentence that served me — the Dreamer and the wide-eyed heart — is cut; the ask's register stays physical, finishable and free of promises.
